source.text: וְהִתְנַבִּ֞י חַגַּ֣י נְבִיָּ֗א וּזְכַרְיָ֤ה בַר־עִדּוֹא֙ נְבִיַּיָּ֔א עַל־יְה֣וּדָיֵ֔א דִּ֥י בִיה֖וּד וּבִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם בְּשֻׁ֛ם אֱלָ֥הּ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עֲלֵיהֽוֹן׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And prophesied Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, the prophets, to the Jews who [were] in Judah and in Jerusalem, in [the] name of [the] God of Israel [who was] over them.

en.L: And Haggai the prophet and Zechariah son of Iddo, the prophets, prophesied to the Jews who were in Judah and in Jerusalem, in the name of the God of Israel, [who was] over them.
en.B: Now the prophets Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo prophesied to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem in the name of the God of Israel, who was over them.
en.R: Then two prophets, Haggai and Zechariah son of Iddo, spoke God's messages to the Jews who lived in Judah and Jerusalem. They spoke in the name of the God of Israel, who ruled over {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people.

es.L: Y profetizaron Hageo el profeta y Zacarías hijo de Ido, los profetas, a los judíos que estaban en Judá y en Jerusalén, en el nombre del Dios de Israel, [que estaba] sobre ellos.
es.B: Los profetas Hageo y Zacarías hijo de Ido profetizaron a los judíos de Judá y de Jerusalén en el nombre del Dios de Israel, que estaba sobre ellos.
es.R: Entonces dos profetas, Hageo y Zacarías hijo de Ido, les comunicaron los mensajes de Dios a los judíos que vivían en Judá y en Jerusalén. Hablaron en el nombre del Dios de Israel, que gobernaba sobre {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} pueblo.

fr.L: Et Aggée le prophète et Zacharie, fils d’Iddo, les prophètes, prophétisèrent aux Juifs qui étaient en Juda et à Jérusalem, au nom du Dieu d’Israël, [qui était] sur eux.
fr.B: Or les prophètes Aggée et Zacharie, fils d’Iddo, prophétisèrent aux Juifs de Juda et de Jérusalem au nom du Dieu d’Israël, qui était sur eux.
fr.R: Alors deux prophètes, Aggée et Zacharie, fils d’Iddo, ont transmis les messages de Dieu aux Juifs qui habitaient en Juda et à Jérusalem. Ils parlaient au nom du Dieu d’Israël, qui régnait sur {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple.

sw.L: Na Hagai nabii na Zekaria mwana wa Ido, manabii, wakatoa unabii kwa Wayahudi waliokuwa Yuda na Yerusalemu, kwa jina la Mungu wa Israeli, [aliyekuwa] juu yao.
sw.B: Basi manabii Hagai na Zekaria mwana wa Ido walitoa unabii kwa Wayahudi waliokuwa Yuda na Yerusalemu kwa jina la Mungu wa Israeli, aliyekuwa juu yao.
sw.R: Kisha manabii wawili, Hagai na Zekaria mwana wa Ido, waliwapa Wayahudi walioishi Yuda na Yerusalemu ujumbe kutoka kwa Mungu. Walisema kwa jina la Mungu wa Israeli, aliyewatawala watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

decisions.choice: Haggai and Zechariah: the two prophets whose books stand in the Bible
decisions.reason: Their messages are kept in the books of Haggai and Zechariah. Both are dated to the second year of King Darius (Haggai 1:1; Zechariah 1:1), about 520 BC, the year named in 4:24. Haggai rebuked the people for living in finished houses while God's house lay in ruins (Haggai 1:4); Zechariah encouraged Zerubbabel that the work would be finished (Zechariah 4:9).

decisions.choice: son of Iddo: of the family of Iddo
decisions.reason: Zechariah 1:1 calls him son of Berechiah, son of Iddo, and Nehemiah 12:16 lists a priestly family of Iddo. Here, as in 6:14, "son" names him by his better-known forebear, as Hebrew and Aramaic often do.

decisions.choice: over them: the God of Israel who was over the people
alternatives: the name that was over them
decisions.reason: The phrase most naturally describes God as the one over the Jews, their Lord and protector. It may also mean that his name was called over them, marking them as his people (compare Jeremiah 14:9). Both readings say the same thing in the end: the prophets spoke with the authority of the God to whom Judah belonged.

decisions.choice: spoke God's messages; who ruled over his people
decisions.reason: Readable says what prophesying is and makes the people explicit as the ones God was over (m3).

decisions.choice: "Hageo", "Zacarías hijo de Ido"
decisions.reason: The prophets in the forms the terms note gives (Zacarías hijo de Ido as 2 Chronicles 9:29 has Iddo).

decisions.choice: "Hagai", "Zekaria mwana wa Ido"
decisions.reason: The terms-note forms: the Old Testament prophet is "Zekaria", kept apart from Matthew 23:35's "Zakaria".

decisions.choice: "Aggée", "Zacharie, fils d'Iddo"
decisions.reason: The French names of the two prophets and of their books, as the terms note settles them.

source.text: בֵּאדַ֡יִן קָ֠מוּ זְרֻבָּבֶ֤ל בַּר־שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵל֙ וְיֵשׁ֣וּעַ בַּר־יֽוֹצָדָ֔ק וְשָׁרִ֣יו לְמִבְנֵ֔א בֵּ֥ית אֱלָהָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירֽוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וְעִמְּה֛וֹן נְבִיַּיָּ֥א דִֽי־אֱלָהָ֖א מְסָעֲדִ֥ין לְהֽוֹן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Then arose Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak and began to build [the] house of God which [is] in Jerusalem; and with them [were] the prophets of God, supporting them.

en.L: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak arose and began to build the house of God which is in Jerusalem, and with them were the prophets of God, supporting them.
en.B: Then Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak set to work and began again to build the house of God in Jerusalem. The prophets of God were with them, helping them.
en.R: So Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel and Jeshua son of Jozadak started again to build God's temple in Jerusalem. God's prophets were with them and helped them.

es.L: Entonces se levantaron Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel y Jesúa hijo de Josadac y comenzaron a edificar la casa de Dios que [está] en Jerusalén, y con ellos [estaban] los profetas de Dios, que los apoyaban.
es.B: Entonces Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel y Jesúa hijo de Josadac se pusieron a trabajar y comenzaron de nuevo a edificar la casa de Dios en Jerusalén. Los profetas de Dios estaban con ellos y los ayudaban.
es.R: Así que Zorobabel hijo de Salatiel y Jesúa hijo de Josadac comenzaron otra vez a construir el templo de Dios en Jerusalén. Los profetas de Dios estaban con ellos y los ayudaban.

fr.L: Alors Zorobabel, fils de Salathiel, et Yeshoua, fils de Yotsadaq, se levèrent et commencèrent à bâtir la maison de Dieu qui est à Jérusalem ; et avec eux [étaient] les prophètes de Dieu, qui les soutenaient.
fr.B: Alors Zorobabel, fils de Salathiel, et Yeshoua, fils de Yotsadaq, se mirent à l’œuvre et recommencèrent à bâtir la maison de Dieu à Jérusalem. Les prophètes de Dieu étaient avec eux et les aidaient.
fr.R: Alors Zorobabel, fils de Salathiel, et Yeshoua, fils de Yotsadaq, ont recommencé à construire le temple de Dieu à Jérusalem. Les prophètes de Dieu étaient avec eux et les aidaient.

sw.L: Ndipo Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli na Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki wakainuka, wakaanza kuijenga nyumba ya Mungu iliyoko Yerusalemu, na pamoja nao walikuwa manabii wa Mungu, wakiwasaidia.
sw.B: Ndipo Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli na Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki walianza kazi, wakaanza tena kuijenga nyumba ya Mungu iliyoko Yerusalemu. Manabii wa Mungu walikuwa pamoja nao, wakiwasaidia.
sw.R: Hivyo Zerubabeli mwana wa Shealtieli na Yeshua mwana wa Yosadaki walianza tena kulijenga hekalu la Mungu huko Yerusalemu. Manabii wa Mungu walikuwa pamoja nao, wakawasaidia.

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel and Jeshua: the governor and the high priest
decisions.reason: Zerubbabel, of David's royal line, and Jeshua the high priest led the first return and laid the foundation (3:2, 8-10). Haggai addresses them by name and calls Zerubbabel governor of Judah (Haggai 1:1, 14).

decisions.choice: arose and began to build: work resumed after it had stopped
decisions.reason: The foundation had been laid years earlier (3:10), but the work stopped under pressure from the peoples around (4:4-5, 24). "Arose" marks a fresh start, which is why Balanced says "began again".

decisions.choice: supporting them: helping, perhaps with their words and their hands
decisions.reason: The verb means to support or sustain. It may mean the encouragement of their prophecies (verse 1; Haggai 2:4) or that they also took part in the work; the text does not say which.

decisions.choice: began again (B); started again (R)
decisions.reason: "Again" is supplied because the work had begun before and been stopped (m2).

source.text: בֵּהּ־זִמְנָא֩ אֲתָ֨א עֲלֵיה֜וֹן תַּ֠תְּנַי פַּחַ֧ת עֲבַֽר־נַהֲרָ֛ה וּשְׁתַ֥ר בּוֹזְנַ֖י וּכְנָוָתְה֑וֹן וְכֵן֙ אָמְרִ֣ין לְהֹ֔ם מַן־שָׂ֨ם לְכֹ֜ם טְעֵ֗ם בַּיְתָ֤א דְנָה֙ לִבְּנֵ֔א וְאֻשַּׁרְנָ֥א דְנָ֖ה לְשַׁכְלָלָֽה׃ס

records.literal_gloss: At it, the time, came to them Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues, and thus [they were] saying to them: Who made for you a decree this house to build and this structure to finish?

en.L: At that time Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues came to them and said thus to them: "Who issued you a decree to build this house and to finish this structure?"
en.B: At that time Tattenai, the governor of the province Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues came to them and asked, "Who gave you an order to build this house and to finish this structure?"
en.R: At that time Tattenai, the governor of the province west of the Euphrates River, came to them with Shethar-bozenai and the other officials. They asked, "Who gave you permission to build this temple and finish it?"

es.L: En aquel tiempo vinieron a ellos Tatenai, gobernador de Más Allá del Río, y Setar-boznai y sus compañeros, y les dijeron así: «¿Quién {{plural_you:les dio|os dio}} orden de edificar esta casa y de terminar esta estructura?».
es.B: En aquel tiempo, Tatenai, gobernador de la provincia de Más Allá del Río, Setar-boznai y sus compañeros vinieron a ellos y les preguntaron: «¿Quién {{plural_you:les dio|os dio}} orden de edificar esta casa y de terminar esta estructura?».
es.R: En ese tiempo, Tatenai, el gobernador de la provincia al oeste del río Éufrates, vino a verlos con Setar-boznai y los demás funcionarios. Les preguntaron: «¿Quién {{plural_you:les dio|os dio}} permiso para construir este templo y terminarlo?».

fr.L: En ce temps-là, Tattenaï, gouverneur d’Au-delà du Fleuve, et Shethar-Boznaï et leurs collègues vinrent vers eux et leur parlèrent ainsi : « Qui vous a donné un décret pour bâtir cette maison et pour achever cette structure ? »
fr.B: En ce temps-là, Tattenaï, gouverneur de la province d’Au-delà du Fleuve, Shethar-Boznaï et leurs collègues vinrent vers eux et leur demandèrent : « Qui vous a donné l’ordre de bâtir cette maison et d’achever cette structure ? »
fr.R: À ce moment-là, Tattenaï, le gouverneur de la province à l’ouest de l’Euphrate, est venu les voir avec Shethar-Boznaï et les autres fonctionnaires. Ils leur ont demandé : « Qui vous a permis de construire ce temple et de le terminer ? »

sw.L: Wakati huo Tatenai, liwali wa Ng'ambo ya Mto, na Shethar-bozenai na wenzao wakawajia, wakawaambia hivi: "Ni nani aliyewapa amri ya kuijenga nyumba hii na kuumaliza ujenzi huu?"
sw.B: Wakati huo Tatenai, liwali wa jimbo la Ng'ambo ya Mto, Shethar-bozenai na wenzao waliwajia, wakawauliza, "Ni nani aliyewapa amri ya kuijenga nyumba hii na kuumaliza ujenzi huu?"
sw.R: Wakati huo Tatenai, liwali wa jimbo lililo magharibi ya mto Frati, aliwajia pamoja na Shethar-bozenai na maafisa wengine. Wakawauliza, "Ni nani aliyewapa ruhusa ya kulijenga hekalu hili na kulimaliza?"

decisions.choice: Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River: the Persian governor of the lands west of the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "Beyond the River" was the Persian name for the province west of the Euphrates, seen from the Persian heartland: Syria, Phoenicia, Samaria and Judah. A governor named Tattenai of this province is known from a Babylonian document of Darius's reign. He was over the local governors such as Zerubbabel.

decisions.choice: a decree: an official order with royal authority
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word means a command or decision. The question is whether the building has the king's authority behind it, since unlicensed building in a subject province could be taken as rebellion (compare 4:12-16).

decisions.choice: this structure: a word of uncertain meaning
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word is rare (also verse 9) and probably borrowed from Persian. It may mean the building's structure as a whole, its walls, or its timber work and fittings. In context it stands beside "this house" and means the work going on at the temple.

decisions.choice: the province west of the Euphrates River
decisions.reason: Readable says where "Beyond the River" was, as the book-wide choice for Ezra does.

decisions.choice: "Tatenai", "Setar-boznai"; "gobernador"
decisions.reason: The names in the forms the terms note gives; the Persian title is "gobernador" at every level.

decisions.choice: "liwali" for the governor (2 Kings 18:24)
decisions.reason: The terms-note word for a Persian governor, used for Tattenai and for Zerubbabel.

decisions.choice: "Tattenaï", "Shethar-Boznaï"
decisions.reason: The names of the two Persian officials for the whole book, as the terms note.

source.text: אֱדַ֥יִן כְּנֵ֖מָא אֲמַ֣רְנָא לְּהֹ֑ם מַן־אִנּוּן֙ שְׁמָהָ֣ת גֻּבְרַיָּ֔א דִּֽי־דְנָ֥ה בִנְיָנָ֖א בָּנַֽיִן׃

records.literal_gloss: Then thus we said to them: What [are] they, [the] names of the men who this building [are] building?

en.L: Then we said to them thus: "What are the names of the men who are building this building?"
en.B: We also asked them, "What are the names of the men who are putting up this building?"
en.R: We also asked them for the names of the men who were doing the building.

es.L: Entonces les dijimos así: «¿Cuáles son los nombres de los hombres que están edificando este edificio?».
es.B: También les preguntamos: «¿Cuáles son los nombres de los hombres que están levantando este edificio?».
es.R: También les pedimos los nombres de los hombres que estaban construyendo.

fr.L: Alors nous leur dîmes ainsi : « Quels sont les noms des hommes qui bâtissent ce bâtiment ? »
fr.B: Nous leur demandâmes aussi : « Quels sont les noms des hommes qui élèvent ce bâtiment ? »
fr.R: Nous leur avons aussi demandé les noms des hommes qui faisaient ce travail de construction.

sw.L: Ndipo tukawaambia hivi: "Ni nini majina ya watu wanaoujenga jengo hili?"
sw.B: Tuliwauliza pia, "Majina ya watu wanaolijenga jengo hili ni nani?"
sw.R: Tuliwauliza pia majina ya watu waliokuwa wakijenga.

decisions.choice: we said: the received text has the first person; old Greek and Syriac read "they said"
decisions.reason: In the Masoretic text the verse slips into "we", as if the officials' report (verses 8-10, "we went", "we asked") were already being quoted. The Greek and Syriac translations have "they said", which continues the narrative of verse 3 with a second question. The Hebrew text governs here; the sense is the same either way: the officials asked for the builders' names (verse 10).

decisions.choice: what are the names: a second question from the officials
alternatives: the Jews told the officials what the names were
decisions.reason: Read with "we", the clause could also be the Jews' reply, with the narrator speaking for them. But verse 10 says the officials asked for the leaders' names in order to write them down, so the clause is best read as the officials' question.

decisions.choice: asked them for the names
decisions.reason: Readable turns the quoted question into a statement; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: "tukawaambia" (we said) kept as the Aramaic has it
decisions.reason: The received text slips into "we", as the meaning decision explains; Swahili keeps the first person at every level, as the English does.

decisions.choice: first person "nous" kept
decisions.reason: The Aramaic has "we said", as if the officials' report were already being quoted; French keeps the first person, as the English does (meaning decision m1). Balanced uses the passé simple of narrative, Readable the passé composé.

source.text: וְעֵ֣ין אֱלָהֲהֹ֗ם הֲוָת֙ עַל־שָׂבֵ֣י יְהוּדָיֵ֔א וְלָא־בַטִּ֣לוּ הִמּ֔וֹ עַד־טַעְמָ֖א לְדָרְיָ֣וֶשׁ יְהָ֑ךְ וֶאֱדַ֛יִן יְתִיב֥וּן נִשְׁתְּוָנָ֖א עַל־דְּנָֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: And [the] eye of their God was on [the] elders of the Jews, and not they made cease them until [the] report to Darius should go and then they should return a letter concerning this.

en.L: But the eye of their God was on the elders of the Jews, and they did not stop them until a report should go to Darius and then a letter should be returned concerning it.
en.B: But the eye of their God was watching over the elders of the Jews, and the officials did not stop them until a report could reach Darius and a written answer about it could come back.
en.R: But God was watching over the leaders of the Jews. So the officials did not stop the work while a report was sent to King Darius and they waited for his answer.

es.L: Pero el ojo de su Dios estaba sobre los ancianos de los judíos, y no los hicieron cesar hasta que el informe llegara a Darío y luego se devolviera una carta acerca de ello.
es.B: Pero el ojo de su Dios velaba sobre los ancianos de los judíos, y los funcionarios no los detuvieron hasta que un informe llegara a Darío y volviera una respuesta por escrito.
es.R: Pero Dios cuidaba a los jefes de los judíos. Por eso los funcionarios no detuvieron la obra mientras se enviaba un informe al rey Darío y esperaban su respuesta.

fr.L: Mais l’œil de leur Dieu était sur les anciens des Juifs, et ils ne les arrêtèrent pas jusqu’à ce qu’un rapport parvienne à Darius et qu’ensuite une lettre soit renvoyée à ce sujet.
fr.B: Mais l’œil de leur Dieu veillait sur les anciens des Juifs, et les fonctionnaires ne les arrêtèrent pas en attendant qu’un rapport parvienne à Darius et qu’une réponse écrite revienne à ce sujet.
fr.R: Mais Dieu veillait sur les chefs des Juifs. Alors les fonctionnaires n’ont pas arrêté le travail pendant qu’on envoyait un rapport au roi Darius et qu’on attendait sa réponse.

sw.L: Lakini jicho la Mungu wao lilikuwa juu ya wazee wa Wayahudi, wala hawakuwazuia mpaka taarifa imfikie Dario na ndipo barua irudishwe kuhusu jambo hilo.
sw.B: Lakini jicho la Mungu wao lilikuwa likiwalinda wazee wa Wayahudi, na maafisa hawakuwazuia mpaka taarifa imfikie Dario na jibu la maandishi kuhusu jambo hilo lirudi.
sw.R: Lakini Mungu alikuwa akiwalinda viongozi wa Wayahudi. Kwa hiyo maafisa hawakuisimamisha kazi wakati taarifa ilipopelekwa kwa Mfalme Dario na walipokuwa wakingoja jibu lake.

decisions.choice: the eye of their God was on them: God watched over them with care
decisions.reason: God's eye on someone means his attention and protection (Psalm 33:18; Ezra 7:6, 28 says the same with God's hand). The writer sees God's care behind the officials' decision to let the work go on.

decisions.choice: Darius: Darius I, king of Persia 522-486 BC
decisions.reason: This is Darius son of Hystaspes, who took the throne in 522 BC after a time of revolt. His second year (4:24; Haggai 1:1) was 520 BC. He organized the empire into provinces with governors and royal records, which fits the search of the archives in 6:1-2.

decisions.choice: they did not stop them: the officials let the building continue while they waited
decisions.reason: The subject is Tattenai and his colleagues, and "them" is the elders. The officials could have halted the work at once; instead they wrote to the king and let it go on.

decisions.choice: the officials
decisions.reason: Balanced names the subject, which the Aramaic leaves as "they" (m3).

decisions.choice: God was watching over the leaders
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of God's eye (m1) and says "leaders" for elders, the heads of the families who led the community.

decisions.choice: "Dios cuidaba" (R); "el ojo de su Dios" (L, B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of God's eye; Readable says what it means (m1), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "Mungu alikuwa akiwalinda" (R); Literal and Balanced keep "jicho la Mungu wao"
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture, as the English Readable does.

source.text: פַּרְשֶׁ֣גֶן אִ֠גַּרְתָּא דִּֽי־שְׁלַ֞ח תַּתְּנַ֣י׀פַּחַ֣ת עֲבַֽר־נַהֲרָ֗ה וּשְׁתַ֤ר בּוֹזְנַי֙ וּכְנָ֣וָתֵ֔הּ אֲפַ֨רְסְכָיֵ֔א דִּ֖י בַּעֲבַ֣ר נַהֲרָ֑ה עַל־דָּרְיָ֖וֶשׁ מַלְכָּֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] copy of the letter which sent Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and his colleagues, the officials who [were] in Beyond the River, to Darius the king.

en.L: The copy of the letter that Tattenai, governor of Beyond the River, and Shethar-bozenai and his colleagues, the officials who were in Beyond the River, sent to Darius the king.
en.B: This is a copy of the letter that Tattenai the governor of Beyond the River, Shethar-bozenai and their colleagues, the officials in the province Beyond the River, sent to King Darius.
en.R: Here is a copy of the letter that Tattenai the governor, Shethar-bozenai and the other officials of the province west of the Euphrates sent to King Darius.

es.L: Copia de la carta que Tatenai, gobernador de Más Allá del Río, y Setar-boznai y sus compañeros, los funcionarios que estaban en Más Allá del Río, enviaron al rey Darío.
es.B: Esta es una copia de la carta que Tatenai, gobernador de Más Allá del Río, Setar-boznai y sus compañeros, los funcionarios de la provincia de Más Allá del Río, enviaron al rey Darío.
es.R: Esta es una copia de la carta que Tatenai, el gobernador, Setar-boznai y los demás funcionarios de la provincia al oeste del Éufrates enviaron al rey Darío.

fr.L: La copie de la lettre que Tattenaï, gouverneur d’Au-delà du Fleuve, et Shethar-Boznaï et ses collègues, les fonctionnaires qui étaient dans Au-delà du Fleuve, envoyèrent au roi Darius.
fr.B: Voici la copie de la lettre que Tattenaï, gouverneur d’Au-delà du Fleuve, Shethar-Boznaï et leurs collègues, les fonctionnaires de la province d’Au-delà du Fleuve, envoyèrent au roi Darius.
fr.R: Voici la copie de la lettre que Tattenaï, le gouverneur, Shethar-Boznaï et les autres fonctionnaires de la province à l’ouest de l’Euphrate ont envoyée au roi Darius.

sw.L: Nakala ya barua ambayo Tatenai, liwali wa Ng'ambo ya Mto, na Shethar-bozenai na wenzake, maafisa waliokuwa Ng'ambo ya Mto, walimpelekea Dario mfalme.
sw.B: Hii ndiyo nakala ya barua ambayo Tatenai liwali wa Ng'ambo ya Mto, Shethar-bozenai na wenzao, maafisa wa jimbo la Ng'ambo ya Mto, walimpelekea Mfalme Dario.
sw.R: Hii ndiyo nakala ya barua ambayo Tatenai liwali, Shethar-bozenai na maafisa wengine wa jimbo lililo magharibi ya mto Frati walimpelekea Mfalme Dario.

decisions.choice: the officials: a Persian word of uncertain meaning
decisions.reason: The word is borrowed from Persian and occurs also in 6:6 (and a similar one in 4:9). Older translations took it as the name of a people. It is now usually understood as a title for a kind of official, perhaps an inspector or envoy. Here it describes Tattenai's colleagues.

decisions.choice: the copy of the letter: the writer quotes the official record
decisions.reason: Ezra 4-7 quotes several royal letters in Aramaic, the language used for government letters across the Persian empire (4:7, 11; 7:11). "Copy" is a Persian loanword for a written copy of a document.

decisions.choice: This is (B); Here is (R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic is a heading, "The copy of the letter"; Balanced and Readable make it a sentence.

source.text: פִּתְגָמָ֖א שְׁלַ֣חוּ עֲל֑וֹהִי וְכִדְנָה֙ כְּתִ֣יב בְּגַוֵּ֔הּ לְדָרְיָ֥וֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֖א שְׁלָמָ֥א כֹֽלָּא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: The report they sent to him, and thus [it was] written in it: To Darius the king, all peace.

en.L: They sent a report to him, and thus it was written in it: "To Darius the king, all peace.
en.B: The report they sent him read as follows: "To King Darius: All peace.
en.R: This is what their report said: "To King Darius. We wish you peace and well-being.

es.L: Le enviaron un informe, y en él estaba escrito así: «Al rey Darío, paz completa.
es.B: El informe que le enviaron decía así: «Al rey Darío: Saludos.
es.R: Esto es lo que decía su informe: «Al rey Darío. Te deseamos paz y bienestar.

fr.L: Ils lui envoyèrent un rapport, et il y était écrit ainsi : « Au roi Darius, toute paix.
fr.B: Le rapport qu’ils lui envoyèrent était rédigé ainsi : « Au roi Darius : Toute paix.
fr.R: Voici ce que disait leur rapport : « Au roi Darius. Nous te souhaitons paix et prospérité.

sw.L: Wakampelekea taarifa, na ndani yake iliandikwa hivi: "Kwa Dario mfalme, amani yote.
sw.B: Taarifa waliyompelekea ilisema hivi: "Kwa Mfalme Dario: Amani yote.
sw.R: Taarifa yao ilisema hivi: "Kwa Mfalme Dario. Tunakutakia amani na mema yote.

decisions.choice: all peace: the greeting of a letter
decisions.reason: A letter of the time began with the name of the one it was sent to and a wish for his peace, that is, his welfare. "Peace" here is the opening greeting, as in other Aramaic letters (4:17; 7:12). The letter runs to the end of verse 17.

decisions.choice: We wish you peace and well-being
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the greeting, keeping "peace" and adding what it meant in a greeting (m1).

decisions.choice: "paz completa" (L); "Saludos" (B); "Te deseamos paz y bienestar" (R)
decisions.reason: The greeting of the Aramaic letters as the terms note sets it; Readable spells out the wish, as the English Readable does. The letter runs to the end of verse 17, and the elders' words quoted inside it (verses 11-16) take “ ”.

decisions.choice: "Amani yote" kept at Balanced; Readable "Tunakutakia amani na mema yote"
decisions.reason: Darius's letter greets with "all peace", which the English keeps at Balanced too; Swahili "amani" carries the wish for welfare.

decisions.choice: "toute paix" (Literal, Balanced); "Nous te souhaitons paix et prospérité" (Readable)
decisions.reason: The terms note gives "Salut" at Balanced for the bare "peace"; here the Aramaic says "all peace", so Balanced keeps "Toute paix", as the English keeps "All peace".

source.text: יְדִ֣יעַ׀לֶהֱוֵ֣א לְמַלְכָּ֗א דִּֽי־אֲזַ֜לְנָא לִיה֤וּד מְדִֽינְתָּא֙ לְבֵית֙ אֱלָהָ֣א רַבָּ֔א וְה֤וּא מִתְבְּנֵא֙ אֶ֣בֶן גְּלָ֔ל וְאָ֖ע מִתְּשָׂ֣ם בְּכֻתְלַיָּ֑א וַעֲבִ֥ידְתָּא דָ֛ךְ אָסְפַּ֥רְנָא מִתְעַבְדָ֖א וּמַצְלַ֥ח בְּיֶדְהֹֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Known let it be to the king that we went to Judah the province to [the] house of the great God, and it [is] being built [with] stones of rolling, and timber [is] being set in the walls, and this work diligently [is] being done and prospers in their hand.

en.L: Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God, and it is being built with huge stones, and timber is being set in the walls; and this work is being done diligently and is prospering in their hand.
en.B: Let it be known to the king that we went to the province of Judah, to the house of the great God. It is being built with large stones, and timbers are being laid in the walls. The work is being carried out diligently and is making good progress in their hands.
en.R: Your Majesty should know that we went to the province of Judah, to the temple of the great God. The people are building it with huge stones and putting beams into the walls. They are working hard, and the work is going well.

es.L: Sepa el rey que fuimos a la provincia de Judá, a la casa del gran Dios, la cual se está edificando con piedras enormes, y se están poniendo maderos en las paredes; y esta obra se hace con diligencia y prospera en sus manos.
es.B: Que el rey sepa que fuimos a la provincia de Judá, a la casa del gran Dios. Se está edificando con grandes piedras, y se están colocando vigas en las paredes. La obra se hace con diligencia y avanza bien en sus manos.
es.R: Queremos informar al rey que fuimos a la provincia de Judá, al templo del gran Dios. La gente lo está construyendo con piedras enormes y está poniendo vigas en las paredes. Trabajan mucho, y la obra va bien.

fr.L: Qu’il soit connu du roi que nous sommes allés dans la province de Juda, à la maison du grand Dieu ; elle se bâtit avec d’énormes pierres, et on pose du bois dans les murs ; et ce travail se fait avec soin et prospère entre leurs mains.
fr.B: Que le roi sache que nous sommes allés dans la province de Juda, à la maison du grand Dieu. On la bâtit avec de grandes pierres, et on pose des poutres dans les murs. Le travail est mené avec soin et progresse bien entre leurs mains.
fr.R: Nous voulons que tu saches, ô roi, que nous sommes allés dans la province de Juda, au temple du grand Dieu. Les gens le construisent avec d’énormes pierres et ils mettent des poutres dans les murs. Ils travaillent dur, et le travail avance bien.

sw.L: Ijulikane kwa mfalme kwamba tulikwenda katika jimbo la Yuda, kwenye nyumba ya Mungu mkuu, nayo inajengwa kwa mawe makubwa, na miti inawekwa katika kuta; na kazi hii inafanywa kwa bidii na inafanikiwa mkononi mwao.
sw.B: Ijulikane kwa mfalme kwamba tulikwenda katika jimbo la Yuda, kwenye nyumba ya Mungu mkuu. Inajengwa kwa mawe makubwa, na boriti zinawekwa katika kuta. Kazi inafanywa kwa bidii na inaendelea vizuri mikononi mwao.
sw.R: Mfalme na ajue kwamba tulikwenda katika jimbo la Yuda, kwenye hekalu la Mungu mkuu. Watu wanalijenga kwa mawe makubwa sana na kuweka boriti katika kuta. Wanafanya kazi kwa bidii, na kazi inaendelea vizuri.

decisions.choice: stones of rolling: very large stones, too heavy to carry
decisions.reason: The phrase means stones that had to be rolled into place (also 6:4), that is, large blocks. It may also mean cut and finished stone. Either way the officials report that this is solid, serious building, not a makeshift shrine.

decisions.choice: timber set in the walls: courses of wood laid between courses of stone
decisions.reason: Building with layers of beams between rows of stone was used for strength (1 Kings 6:36; 7:12; compare Ezra 6:4). The officials describe the method they saw.

decisions.choice: the great God: the officials' own respectful words
decisions.reason: The Persian officials call the God of the Jews "the great God", using the title the Jews themselves used (verse 11). It is the language of an official report, not a confession of their own faith.

decisions.choice: diligently: with care and with speed
decisions.reason: The Persian loanword means exactly, carefully, or promptly. It appears again in Darius's reply (6:8, 12, 13), where the king orders that his decree be carried out with the same care.

decisions.choice: Your Majesty should know
decisions.reason: Readable puts the formal opening "Let it be known to the king" in plain terms of address.

source.text: אֱדַ֗יִן שְׁאֵ֨לְנָא֙ לְשָׂבַיָּ֣א אִלֵּ֔ךְ כְּנֵ֖מָא אֲמַ֣רְנָא לְּהֹ֑םמַן־שָׂ֨ם לְכֹ֜ם טְעֵ֗ם בַּיְתָ֤א דְנָה֙ לְמִבְנְיָ֔ה וְאֻשַּׁרְנָ֥א דְנָ֖ה לְשַׁכְלָלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Then we asked those elders; thus we said to them: Who made for you a decree this house to build and this structure to finish?

en.L: Then we asked those elders; thus we said to them: "Who issued you a decree to build this house and to finish this structure?"
en.B: We asked those elders, "Who gave you an order to build this house and to finish this structure?"
en.R: We asked their leaders, "Who gave you permission to build this temple and finish it?"

es.L: Entonces preguntamos a esos ancianos; les dijimos así: “¿Quién {{plural_you:les dio|os dio}} orden de edificar esta casa y de terminar esta estructura?”.
es.B: Les preguntamos a esos ancianos: “¿Quién {{plural_you:les dio|os dio}} orden de edificar esta casa y de terminar esta estructura?”.
es.R: Les preguntamos a sus jefes: “¿Quién {{plural_you:les dio|os dio}} permiso para construir este templo y terminarlo?”.

fr.L: Alors nous avons interrogé ces anciens ; nous leur avons dit ainsi : “Qui vous a donné un décret pour bâtir cette maison et pour achever cette structure ?”
fr.B: Nous avons interrogé ces anciens : “Qui vous a donné l’ordre de bâtir cette maison et d’achever cette structure ?”
fr.R: Nous avons demandé à leurs chefs : “Qui vous a permis de construire ce temple et de le terminer ?”

sw.L: Ndipo tukawauliza wazee hao; tukawaambia hivi: "Ni nani aliyewapa amri ya kuijenga nyumba hii na kuumaliza ujenzi huu?"
sw.B: Tuliwauliza wazee hao, "Ni nani aliyewapa amri ya kuijenga nyumba hii na kuumaliza ujenzi huu?"
sw.R: Tuliwauliza viongozi wao, "Ni nani aliyewapa ruhusa ya kulijenga hekalu hili na kulimaliza?"

decisions.choice: this structure: as in verse 3
decisions.reason: The officials repeat the question of verse 3 word for word; the rare word is discussed there.

decisions.choice: permission
decisions.reason: Readable says "permission" because the officials wanted to know whether the king had authorized the work (verse 3).

decisions.choice: “ ” inside the letter
decisions.reason: The officials' report is already inside quotation marks, so the questions and answers it quotes take the inner French marks “ ” (French style guide, section 4), where the English uses single quotation marks.

source.text: וְאַ֧ף שְׁמָהָתְהֹ֛ם שְׁאֵ֥לְנָא לְּהֹ֖םלְהוֹדָעוּתָ֑ךְ דִּ֛י נִכְתֻּ֥ב שֻׁם־גֻּבְרַיָּ֖א דִּ֥י בְרָאשֵׁיהֹֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And also their names we asked them, to make known to you, that we might write [the] name[s] of the men who [are] at their heads.

en.L: And we also asked them their names, to make them known to you, so that we might write down the names of the men who are at their head.
en.B: We also asked them their names, so that we could inform you by writing down the names of the men who are their leaders.
en.R: We also asked for the names of their leaders, so that we could write them down and send them to you.

es.L: Y también les preguntamos sus nombres, para hacértelos saber, para escribir los nombres de los hombres que están a la cabeza de ellos.
es.B: También les preguntamos sus nombres, para informarte por escrito de los nombres de los hombres que son sus jefes.
es.R: También les pedimos los nombres de sus jefes, para escribirlos y enviártelos.

fr.L: Et nous leur avons aussi demandé leurs noms, pour te les faire connaître, afin d’écrire les noms des hommes qui sont à leur tête.
fr.B: Nous leur avons aussi demandé leurs noms, afin de t’informer en écrivant les noms des hommes qui les dirigent.
fr.R: Nous avons aussi demandé les noms de leurs chefs, pour pouvoir les écrire et te les envoyer.

sw.L: Na pia tukawauliza majina yao, ili tukujulishe, ili tuandike majina ya watu walio vichwa vyao.
sw.B: Tuliwauliza pia majina yao, ili tukujulishe kwa kuandika majina ya watu walio viongozi wao.
sw.R: Tuliuliza pia majina ya viongozi wao, ili tuyaandike na kukutumia.

decisions.choice: to write the names of the leaders: the men answerable to the king
decisions.reason: A list of names told the king who was responsible for the work. If the building proved unlawful, those named could be held to account; if it was lawful, the king knew whom his orders concerned.

decisions.choice: so that we could inform you by writing down (B); write them down and send them to you (R)
decisions.reason: The Aramaic gives two purposes side by side, to inform the king and to write the names; Balanced and Readable join them so the order of events is clear.

source.text: וּכְנֵ֥מָא פִתְגָמָ֖א הֲתִיב֣וּנָא לְמֵמַ֑ר אֲנַ֣חְנָא הִמּ֡וֹ עַבְדוֹהִי֩ דִֽי־אֱלָ֨הּ שְׁמַיָּ֜א וְאַרְעָ֗א וּבָנַ֤יִן בַּיְתָא֙ דִּֽי־הֲוָ֨א בְנֵ֜ה מִקַּדְמַ֤ת דְּנָה֙ שְׁנִ֣ין שַׂגִּיאָ֔ן וּמֶ֤לֶךְ לְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ רַ֔ב בְּנָ֖הִי וְשַׁכְלְלֵֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And thus [the] word they returned to us, saying: We, we [are] servants of the God of the heavens and the earth, and [we are] building the house that was built from before this many years, and a great king of Israel built it and finished it.

en.L: And thus they returned word to us, saying, 'We are the slaves of the God of heaven and earth, and we are building the house that was built many years before this, which a great king of Israel built and finished.
en.B: This is the answer they gave us: 'We are the servants of the God of heaven and earth, and we are rebuilding the house that was built many years ago, which a great king of Israel built and completed.
en.R: This is how they answered us: 'We serve the God of heaven and earth. We are rebuilding the temple that was first built many years ago. A great king of Israel built it and finished it.

es.L: Y así nos respondieron, diciendo: “Nosotros somos esclavos del Dios de los cielos y de la tierra, y edificamos la casa que fue edificada hace muchos años, la cual edificó y terminó un gran rey de Israel.
es.B: Esta es la respuesta que nos dieron: “Somos siervos del Dios de los cielos y de la tierra, y estamos reedificando la casa que fue edificada hace muchos años, la que edificó y terminó un gran rey de Israel.
es.R: Esto es lo que nos respondieron: “Servimos al Dios de los cielos y de la tierra. Estamos reconstruyendo el templo que se construyó por primera vez hace muchos años. Un gran rey de Israel lo construyó y lo terminó.

fr.L: Et voici la réponse qu’ils nous ont rendue : “Nous sommes les esclaves du Dieu des cieux et de la terre, et nous bâtissons la maison qui avait été bâtie il y a bien des années, et qu’un grand roi d’Israël avait bâtie et achevée.
fr.B: Voici la réponse qu’ils nous ont donnée : “Nous sommes les serviteurs du Dieu des cieux et de la terre, et nous rebâtissons la maison qui avait été bâtie il y a bien des années, et qu’un grand roi d’Israël avait construite et achevée.
fr.R: Voici ce qu’ils nous ont répondu : “Nous servons le Dieu du ciel et de la terre. Nous reconstruisons le temple qui avait été construit il y a bien des années. Un grand roi d’Israël l’avait construit et terminé.

sw.L: Nao wakaturudishia jibu hivi, wakisema, 'Sisi ni watumwa wa Mungu wa mbingu na nchi, nasi tunaijenga nyumba iliyojengwa miaka mingi kabla ya hii, ambayo mfalme mkuu wa Israeli aliijenga na kuimaliza.
sw.B: Hili ndilo jibu walilotupa: 'Sisi ni watumishi wa Mungu wa mbingu na nchi, nasi tunaijenga upya nyumba iliyojengwa miaka mingi iliyopita, ambayo mfalme mkuu wa Israeli aliijenga na kuikamilisha.
sw.R: Walitujibu hivi: 'Sisi tunamtumikia Mungu wa mbingu na nchi. Tunalijenga upya hekalu lililojengwa kwanza miaka mingi iliyopita. Mfalme mkuu wa Israeli alilijenga na kulimaliza.

decisions.choice: his servants: those who belong to God and work for him
decisions.reason: The Aramaic word is the same as the Hebrew word for a slave or servant: one who belongs to a master, not a hired worker. The elders answer the king's officials by naming the master they serve, the God of heaven and earth, whose authority stands above any earthly ruler.

decisions.choice: the God of heaven and earth: the creator who rules over all
decisions.reason: The elders do not speak of a local god of Judah but of the God who made heaven and earth. "The God of heaven" is the title used for Israel's God in the Persian documents of Ezra (1:2; 6:9-10; 7:12, 21).

decisions.choice: a great king of Israel: Solomon
decisions.reason: Solomon built the first temple about 960 BC (1 Kings 6:1, 37-38). The elders point out that the house is no new venture but the restoration of an ancient one, which would matter to a Persian king who respected old sanctuaries.

decisions.choice: servants (B); We serve (R)
decisions.reason: Following the project's rule, Literal says "slaves" and Balanced and Readable "servants"; the meaning decision keeps the sense of belonging to a master.

decisions.choice: rebuilding
decisions.reason: "Building" a house that had stood before means rebuilding it; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: "esclavos" (L); "siervos" (B); "Servimos" (R)
decisions.reason: The project's rule for this word, as in the English: "esclavo" at Literal, "siervo" at Balanced; the meaning decision keeps the sense of belonging to a master.

decisions.choice: "watumwa" (L), "watumishi" (B), "tunamtumikia" (R); the elders' reply set in single quotation marks inside the letter
decisions.reason: The project's rule for this word; the reply is quoted inside the officials' letter, so it takes the inner quotation marks.

source.text: לָהֵ֗ן מִן־דִּ֨י הַרְגִּ֤זוּ אֲבָהֳתַ֨נָא֙ לֶאֱלָ֣הּ שְׁמַיָּ֔א יְהַ֣ב הִמּ֔וֹ בְּיַ֛ד נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֥ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל כַּסְדָּאָ֑ה וּבַיְתָ֤ה דְנָה֙ סַתְרֵ֔הּ וְעַמָּ֖ה הַגְלִ֥י לְבָבֶֽל׃ס

records.literal_gloss: But because our fathers angered the God of the heavens, he gave them into [the] hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, and this house he destroyed and the people he exiled to Babylon.

en.L: But because our fathers angered the God of heaven, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house and carried the people away into exile to Babylon.
en.B: But because our ancestors made the God of heaven angry, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} handed them over to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, the Chaldean, who destroyed this house and took the people into exile in Babylon.
en.R: But our ancestors made the God of heaven angry. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let Nebuchadnezzar, the Chaldean king of Babylon, defeat them. Nebuchadnezzar destroyed this temple and took the people away as captives to Babylon.

es.L: Pero porque nuestros padres provocaron a ira al Dios de los cielos, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los entregó en mano de Nabucodonosor rey de Babilonia, el caldeo, el cual destruyó esta casa y llevó al pueblo cautivo a Babilonia.
es.B: Pero como nuestros antepasados hicieron enojar al Dios de los cielos, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} los entregó a Nabucodonosor rey de Babilonia, el caldeo, quien destruyó esta casa y llevó al pueblo al destierro en Babilonia.
es.R: Pero nuestros antepasados hicieron enojar al Dios de los cielos. Por eso {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} dejó que Nabucodonosor, el rey de Babilonia, los venciera. Nabucodonosor destruyó este templo y se llevó al pueblo prisionero a Babilonia.

fr.L: Mais parce que nos pères ont irrité le Dieu des cieux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a livrés entre les mains de Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, le Chaldéen, qui a détruit cette maison et a déporté le peuple à Babylone.
fr.B: Mais parce que nos ancêtres ont mis en colère le Dieu des cieux, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les a livrés à Nabuchodonosor, roi de Babylone, le Chaldéen, qui a détruit cette maison et a emmené le peuple en exil à Babylone.
fr.R: Mais nos ancêtres ont mis en colère le Dieu du ciel. Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a laissé Nabuchodonosor, le roi chaldéen de Babylone, les vaincre. Nabuchodonosor a détruit ce temple et il a emmené le peuple prisonnier à Babylone.

sw.L: Lakini kwa sababu baba zetu walimkasirisha Mungu wa mbinguni, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliwatia mkononi mwa Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli, Mkaldayo, aliyeiharibu nyumba hii na kuwahamisha watu mpaka Babeli.
sw.B: Lakini kwa sababu wazee wetu walimkasirisha Mungu wa mbinguni, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aliwatia mikononi mwa Nebukadneza mfalme wa Babeli, Mkaldayo, aliyeiharibu nyumba hii na kuwachukua watu mateka mpaka Babeli.
sw.R: Lakini wazee wetu walimkasirisha Mungu wa mbinguni. Kwa hiyo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alimwacha Nebukadneza, mfalme wa Babeli Mkaldayo, awashinde. Nebukadneza aliliharibu hekalu hili na kuwachukua watu mateka mpaka Babeli.

decisions.choice: because our fathers angered God, he gave them over: the exile was God's judgment
decisions.reason: The elders admit that the temple was not lost because their God was weak but because he gave his people over for their sin, as the prophets had warned (2 Kings 24:3-4; 2 Chronicles 36:15-17). The same God now allows its rebuilding.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar the Chaldean: the king of Babylon who destroyed Jerusalem in 587/586 BC
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar II ruled Babylon 605-562 BC. The Chaldeans were the people from southern Mesopotamia whose dynasty ruled Babylon in his time. His army burned the temple (2 Kings 25:8-9).

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the earlier generations, men and women; Balanced and Readable say "ancestors".

decisions.choice: let Nebuchadnezzar defeat them
decisions.reason: Readable explains "gave them into the hand", an idiom for handing someone over to an enemy's power.

decisions.choice: "el caldeo" (L, B); left out at Readable
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans are "caldeos" at Literal and Balanced and "babilonios" at Readable (terms note); here Readable already says "rey de Babilonia", so the word is not repeated.

decisions.choice: "wazee wetu" (B, R) for "fathers"; Literal "baba zetu"
decisions.reason: "Fathers" means the earlier generations; "wazee wetu" is the ordinary Swahili for forebears and includes women.

decisions.choice: passé composé ("ont irrité", "a détruit")
decisions.reason: The elders' answer is speech quoted inside a letter, so the history it tells takes the passé composé at every level, as speech does.

source.text: בְּרַם֙ בִּשְׁנַ֣ת חֲדָ֔ה לְכ֥וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֖א דִּ֣י בָבֶ֑ל כּ֤וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּא֙ שָׂ֣ם טְעֵ֔ם בֵּית־אֱלָהָ֥א דְנָ֖ה לִבְּנֵֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: Nevertheless, in year one of Cyrus king of Babylon, Cyrus the king made a decree this house of God to build.

en.L: However, in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, Cyrus the king issued a decree to build this house of God.
en.B: However, in the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon, King Cyrus issued a decree that this house of God should be rebuilt.
en.R: But in the first year that Cyrus was king of Babylon, he gave an order that this temple of God should be built again.

es.L: Sin embargo, en el primer año de Ciro rey de Babilonia, el rey Ciro dio orden de edificar esta casa de Dios.
es.B: Sin embargo, en el primer año de Ciro rey de Babilonia, el rey Ciro dio un decreto para que esta casa de Dios fuera reedificada.
es.R: Pero en el primer año en que Ciro fue rey de Babilonia, dio una orden para que este templo de Dios se construyera de nuevo.

fr.L: Cependant, la première année de Cyrus, roi de Babylone, le roi Cyrus a donné un décret pour bâtir cette maison de Dieu.
fr.B: Cependant, la première année de Cyrus, roi de Babylone, le roi Cyrus a donné l’ordre de rebâtir cette maison de Dieu.
fr.R: Mais la première année où Cyrus a été roi de Babylone, il a donné l’ordre de reconstruire ce temple de Dieu.

sw.L: Lakini, katika mwaka wa kwanza wa Koreshi mfalme wa Babeli, Koreshi mfalme alitoa amri ya kuijenga nyumba hii ya Mungu.
sw.B: Lakini katika mwaka wa kwanza wa Koreshi mfalme wa Babeli, Mfalme Koreshi alitoa amri kwamba nyumba hii ya Mungu ijengwe upya.
sw.R: Lakini katika mwaka wa kwanza wa Koreshi kuwa mfalme wa Babeli, alitoa agizo kwamba hekalu hili la Mungu lijengwe tena.

decisions.choice: the first year of Cyrus king of Babylon: 539/538 BC
decisions.reason: Cyrus the Persian took Babylon in 539 BC; his first year as its king began in 538 BC. The decree is the one recorded in 1:1-4. The elders call him king of Babylon, the title that mattered for the land Babylon had ruled.

decisions.choice: rebuilt (B); built again (R)
decisions.reason: The decree was to build the house again on its old site; Balanced and Readable say so, as in verse 11.

source.text: וְ֠אַף מָאנַיָּ֣א דִֽי־בֵית־אֱלָהָא֮ דִּ֣י דַהֲבָ֣ה וְכַסְפָּא֒ דִּ֣י נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּ֗ר הַנְפֵּק֙ מִן־הֵֽיכְלָא֙ דִּ֣י בִֽירוּשְׁלֶ֔ם וְהֵיבֵ֣ל הִמּ֔וֹ לְהֵיכְלָ֖א דִּ֣י בָבֶ֑ל הַנְפֵּ֨ק הִמּ֜וֹ כּ֣וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּ֗א מִן־הֵֽיכְלָא֙ דִּ֣י בָבֶ֔ל וִיהִ֨יבוּ֙ לְשֵׁשְׁבַּצַּ֣ר שְׁמֵ֔הּ דִּ֥י פֶחָ֖ה שָׂמֵֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And also the vessels of the house of God of gold and silver which Nebuchadnezzar brought out from the temple which [was] in Jerusalem and carried them to the temple of Babylon, these brought out Cyrus the king from the temple of Babylon, and they were given to [one], Sheshbazzar [was] his name, whom he had made governor.

en.L: And also the vessels of gold and silver of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken out of the temple that was in Jerusalem and brought to the temple of Babylon, these Cyrus the king brought out from the temple of Babylon, and they were given to one whose name was Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor.
en.B: King Cyrus also took out of the temple in Babylon the gold and silver vessels of the house of God, which Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple in Jerusalem and brought to the temple in Babylon. He handed them over to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had appointed governor.
en.R: Nebuchadnezzar had taken the gold and silver bowls and other objects from God's temple in Jerusalem and put them in the temple in Babylon. But King Cyrus took them out of that temple and gave them to a man named Sheshbazzar, whom he had made governor.

es.L: Y también los utensilios de oro y de plata de la casa de Dios, que Nabucodonosor había sacado del templo que [estaba] en Jerusalén y había llevado al templo de Babilonia, el rey Ciro los sacó del templo de Babilonia, y fueron entregados a uno llamado Sesbasar, a quien había nombrado gobernador.
es.B: El rey Ciro también sacó del templo de Babilonia los utensilios de oro y de plata de la casa de Dios, que Nabucodonosor había sacado del templo de Jerusalén y había llevado al templo de Babilonia. Se los entregó a un hombre llamado Sesbasar, a quien había nombrado gobernador.
es.R: Nabucodonosor había sacado del templo de Dios en Jerusalén las vasijas y los demás objetos de oro y de plata, y los había puesto en el templo de Babilonia. Pero el rey Ciro los sacó de aquel templo y se los dio a un hombre llamado Sesbasar, a quien había nombrado gobernador.

fr.L: Et aussi les ustensiles d’or et d’argent de la maison de Dieu, que Nabuchodonosor avait enlevés du temple qui était à Jérusalem et emportés au temple de Babylone, le roi Cyrus les a fait sortir du temple de Babylone, et ils ont été remis à un [homme] nommé Sheshbatsar, qu’il avait établi gouverneur.
fr.B: Le roi Cyrus a aussi fait sortir du temple de Babylone les ustensiles d’or et d’argent de la maison de Dieu, que Nabuchodonosor avait enlevés du temple de Jérusalem et emportés au temple de Babylone. Il les a remis à un homme nommé Sheshbatsar, qu’il avait établi gouverneur.
fr.R: Nabuchodonosor avait pris les coupes et les autres objets en or et en argent du temple de Dieu à Jérusalem, et il les avait mis dans le temple de Babylone. Mais le roi Cyrus les a sortis de ce temple et les a donnés à un homme nommé Sheshbatsar, qu’il avait nommé gouverneur.

sw.L: Na pia vyombo vya dhahabu na fedha vya nyumba ya Mungu, ambavyo Nebukadneza alikuwa amevitoa katika hekalu lililokuwa Yerusalemu na kuviingiza katika hekalu la Babeli, hivyo Koreshi mfalme alivitoa katika hekalu la Babeli, navyo vikapewa mtu mmoja aitwaye Sheshbaza, ambaye alikuwa amemfanya liwali.
sw.B: Mfalme Koreshi pia alivitoa katika hekalu la Babeli vyombo vya dhahabu na fedha vya nyumba ya Mungu, ambavyo Nebukadneza alikuwa amevichukua kutoka hekalu la Yerusalemu na kuviingiza katika hekalu la Babeli. Alimkabidhi mtu mmoja aitwaye Sheshbaza, ambaye alikuwa amemweka kuwa liwali.
sw.R: Nebukadneza alikuwa amechukua mabakuli na vitu vingine vya dhahabu na fedha kutoka hekalu la Mungu huko Yerusalemu na kuviweka katika hekalu la Babeli. Lakini Mfalme Koreshi alivitoa katika hekalu hilo, akampa mtu mmoja aitwaye Sheshbaza, ambaye alikuwa amemfanya liwali.

decisions.choice: the temple of Babylon: the shrine of Babylon's god
decisions.reason: Conquerors placed the sacred objects of defeated peoples in the temple of their own god as trophies (compare 1 Samuel 5:2; Daniel 1:2). Returning them was a public act: it showed that Cyrus restored the worship of the gods of conquered peoples, and for Israel it fulfilled God's promise (1:7-11; Jeremiah 27:21-22).

decisions.choice: Sheshbazzar the governor: the leader of the first return
decisions.reason: Sheshbazzar is called "the prince of Judah" in 1:8 and received the vessels then (1:7-11). Here Cyrus is said to have made him governor. How he relates to Zerubbabel, who led the people at the same time (2:2; 3:8), the text does not say.

decisions.choice: vessels: the temple's sacred utensils
decisions.reason: The word covers all kinds of containers and implements used in worship; 1:9-10 lists basins, bowls and knives.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar had taken ... But King Cyrus took them out
decisions.reason: Readable tells the events in the order they happened, in two sentences.

source.text: וַאֲמַר־לֵ֓הּ׀אֵ֚ל מָֽאנַיָּ֔א שֵׂ֚א אֵֽזֶל־אֲחֵ֣ת הִמּ֔וֹ בְּהֵיכְלָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וּבֵ֥ית אֱלָהָ֖א יִתְבְּנֵ֥א עַל־אַתְרֵֽהּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him: These vessels take, go, deposit them in the temple which [is] in Jerusalem, and [the] house of God let it be built on its place.

en.L: And he said to him, "Take these vessels; go, deposit them in the temple that is in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be built on its place."
en.B: Cyrus told him, "Take these vessels, go and put them in the temple in Jerusalem, and let the house of God be rebuilt on its original site."
en.R: Cyrus told him, "Take these objects and go. Put them in the temple in Jerusalem, and rebuild God's temple where it stood before."

es.L: Y le dijo: ‘Toma estos utensilios, ve, deposítalos en el templo que [está] en Jerusalén, y que la casa de Dios sea edificada en su lugar’.
es.B: Ciro le dijo: ‘Toma estos utensilios, ve y ponlos en el templo de Jerusalén, y que la casa de Dios sea reedificada en su sitio’.
es.R: Ciro le dijo: ‘Toma estos objetos y ve. Ponlos en el templo de Jerusalén, y reconstruye el templo de Dios donde estaba antes’.

fr.L: Et il lui a dit : ‘Prends ces ustensiles, va, dépose-les dans le temple qui est à Jérusalem, et que la maison de Dieu soit bâtie à sa place.’
fr.B: Cyrus lui a dit : ‘Prends ces ustensiles, va les déposer dans le temple de Jérusalem, et que la maison de Dieu soit rebâtie sur son ancien emplacement.’
fr.R: Cyrus lui a dit : ‘Prends ces objets et va. Mets-les dans le temple de Jérusalem, et reconstruis le temple de Dieu là où il se trouvait avant.’

sw.L: Naye akamwambia, "Chukua vyombo hivi; nenda, uviweke katika hekalu lililoko Yerusalemu, na nyumba ya Mungu ijengwe mahali pake."
sw.B: Koreshi akamwambia, "Chukua vyombo hivi, uende ukaviweke katika hekalu lililoko Yerusalemu, na nyumba ya Mungu ijengwe upya mahali ilipokuwa."
sw.R: Koreshi akamwambia, "Chukua vitu hivi uende. Viweke katika hekalu huko Yerusalemu, na ulijenge upya hekalu la Mungu mahali lilipokuwa zamani."

decisions.choice: on its place: on the same site as before
decisions.reason: The house was to stand where Solomon's temple had stood (also 2:68; 6:7). The site itself was holy, which is why the returned exiles built the altar "on its foundations" (3:3).

decisions.choice: Cyrus told him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speaker, who is the "he" of the Aramaic.

decisions.choice: ‘ ’ for Cyrus's words
decisions.reason: Cyrus's words are quoted by the elders, who are quoted in the officials' letter, so they take the third level of Spanish quotation marks, as the terms note sets them (« », “ ”, ‘ ’).

decisions.choice: Cyrus's words in double quotation marks inside the elders' single-quoted reply, stored straight as in English
decisions.reason: The English records reuse double marks at the third level of quotation here; Swahili follows the English record so the nesting stays the same in both.

source.text: אֱדַ֨יִן֙ שֵׁשְׁבַּצַּ֣ר דֵּ֔ךְ אֲתָ֗א יְהַ֧ב אֻשַּׁיָּ֛א דִּי־בֵ֥ית אֱלָהָ֖א דִּ֣י בִירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וּמִן־אֱדַ֧יִן וְעַד־כְּעַ֛ן מִתְבְּנֵ֖א וְלָ֥א שְׁלִֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Then this Sheshbazzar came, he laid the foundations of the house of God which [is] in Jerusalem, and from then and until now [it is] being built and not [is it] finished.

en.L: Then this Sheshbazzar came [and] laid the foundations of the house of God that is in Jerusalem, and from then until now it has been under construction and is not finished.'
en.B: So this Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of the house of God in Jerusalem. From that time until now it has been under construction, and it is still not finished.'
en.R: So Sheshbazzar came and laid the foundations of God's temple in Jerusalem. It has been under construction from that time until now, but it is not finished yet.'

es.L: Entonces este Sesbasar vino [y] puso los cimientos de la casa de Dios que [está] en Jerusalén, y desde entonces hasta ahora se está edificando y no está terminada”.
es.B: Así que este Sesbasar vino y puso los cimientos de la casa de Dios en Jerusalén. Desde entonces hasta ahora se ha estado edificando, y todavía no está terminada”.
es.R: Así que Sesbasar vino y puso los cimientos del templo de Dios en Jerusalén. Desde entonces hasta ahora se ha estado construyendo, pero todavía no está terminado”.

fr.L: Alors ce Sheshbatsar est venu [et] a posé les fondations de la maison de Dieu qui est à Jérusalem, et depuis lors jusqu’à maintenant elle est en construction et n’est pas achevée.”
fr.B: Ce Sheshbatsar est donc venu et a posé les fondations de la maison de Dieu à Jérusalem. Depuis ce temps jusqu’à maintenant, elle est en construction, et elle n’est toujours pas achevée.”
fr.R: Sheshbatsar est donc venu et a posé les fondations du temple de Dieu à Jérusalem. Depuis ce moment jusqu’à maintenant, on le construit, mais il n’est pas encore terminé.”

sw.L: Ndipo Sheshbaza huyo akaja [na] kuiweka misingi ya nyumba ya Mungu iliyoko Yerusalemu, na tangu wakati huo mpaka sasa imekuwa ikijengwa, wala haijamalizika.'
sw.B: Hivyo Sheshbaza huyo alikuja, akaiweka misingi ya nyumba ya Mungu iliyoko Yerusalemu. Tangu wakati huo mpaka sasa imekuwa ikijengwa, na bado haijamalizika.'
sw.R: Hivyo Sheshbaza alikuja, akaiweka misingi ya hekalu la Mungu huko Yerusalemu. Limekuwa likijengwa tangu wakati huo mpaka sasa, lakini bado halijamalizika.'

decisions.choice: Sheshbazzar laid the foundations: he led the work that 3:8-10 describes
decisions.reason: Chapter 3 tells of Zerubbabel and Jeshua leading the laying of the foundation. The elders credit it to Sheshbazzar, the governor appointed by Cyrus, whose name carried weight with the Persian court. He may have begun the work under his authority while Zerubbabel led it on site, or the two names may belong to the same period of leadership seen from two sides; the text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: from then until now it is being built and is not finished: the work has never been completed
decisions.reason: The elders present the work as one continuous project begun under Cyrus's decree, so that it needed no new permission. They pass over the years when it stood still (4:24).

source.text: וּכְעַ֞ן הֵ֧ן עַל־מַלְכָּ֣א טָ֗ב יִ֠תְבַּקַּר בְּבֵ֨ית גִּנְזַיָּ֜א דִּי־מַלְכָּ֣א תַמָּה֮ דִּ֣י בְּבָבֶל֒ הֵ֣ן אִיתַ֗י דִּֽי־מִן־כּ֤וֹרֶשׁ מַלְכָּא֙ שִׂ֣ים טְעֵ֔ם לְמִבְנֵ֛א בֵּית־אֱלָהָ֥א דֵ֖ךְ בִּירוּשְׁלֶ֑ם וּרְע֥וּת מַלְכָּ֛א עַל־דְּנָ֖ה יִשְׁלַ֥ח עֲלֶֽינָא׃ס

records.literal_gloss: And now, if to the king [it is] good, let it be searched in the house of the treasures of the king there which [is] in Babylon, whether there is [that] from Cyrus the king a decree was made to build this house of God in Jerusalem; and the will of the king concerning this let him send to us.

en.L: And now, if it seems good to the king, let a search be made in the king's treasure house there in Babylon, whether it is so that a decree was issued by Cyrus the king to build this house of God in Jerusalem; and let the king send us his will concerning this."
en.B: Now, if it pleases the king, let a search be made in the royal archives in Babylon to see whether King Cyrus really issued a decree to rebuild this house of God in Jerusalem. Then let the king send us his decision on this matter."
en.R: Now, if Your Majesty agrees, please have someone search the royal records in Babylon. See whether King Cyrus really gave an order to rebuild this temple of God in Jerusalem. Then please tell us what you want us to do about this."

es.L: Y ahora, si al rey le parece bien, que se busque en la casa de los tesoros del rey, allí en Babilonia, si es así que el rey Ciro dio orden de edificar esta casa de Dios en Jerusalén; y que el rey nos envíe su voluntad acerca de esto».
es.B: Ahora, si le parece bien al rey, que se busque en los archivos reales de Babilonia para ver si de verdad el rey Ciro dio un decreto para reedificar esta casa de Dios en Jerusalén. Luego, que el rey nos envíe su decisión sobre este asunto».
es.R: Ahora, oh rey, si te parece bien, por favor manda buscar en los registros reales de Babilonia. Que se vea si de verdad el rey Ciro dio una orden para reconstruir este templo de Dios en Jerusalén. Luego, por favor, dinos qué quieres que hagamos en este asunto».

fr.L: Et maintenant, si cela semble bon au roi, qu’on fasse des recherches dans la maison des trésors du roi, là, à Babylone, [pour savoir] s’il est vrai qu’un décret a été donné par le roi Cyrus pour bâtir cette maison de Dieu à Jérusalem ; et que le roi nous envoie sa volonté à ce sujet. »
fr.B: Maintenant, s’il plaît au roi, qu’on fasse des recherches dans les archives royales à Babylone, pour voir si le roi Cyrus a vraiment donné l’ordre de rebâtir cette maison de Dieu à Jérusalem. Que le roi nous envoie ensuite sa décision sur cette affaire. »
fr.R: Maintenant, si tu es d’accord, ô roi, fais chercher dans les archives royales à Babylone. Vois si le roi Cyrus a vraiment donné l’ordre de reconstruire ce temple de Dieu à Jérusalem. Ensuite, dis-nous, s’il te plaît, ce que tu veux que nous fassions à ce sujet. »

sw.L: Na sasa, ikimpendeza mfalme, utafutaji na ufanyike katika nyumba ya hazina ya mfalme huko Babeli, kama ni kweli kwamba amri ilitolewa na Koreshi mfalme ya kuijenga nyumba hii ya Mungu huko Yerusalemu; na mfalme atupelekee mapenzi yake kuhusu jambo hili."
sw.B: Basi sasa, ikimpendeza mfalme, utafutaji ufanyike katika kumbukumbu za kifalme huko Babeli, ili kuona kama kweli Mfalme Koreshi alitoa amri ya kuijenga upya nyumba hii ya Mungu huko Yerusalemu. Kisha mfalme atupelekee uamuzi wake kuhusu jambo hili."
sw.R: Sasa, mfalme akikubali, tafadhali agiza mtu azitafute kumbukumbu za kifalme huko Babeli. Aone kama kweli Mfalme Koreshi alitoa agizo la kulijenga upya hekalu hili la Mungu huko Yerusalemu. Kisha tafadhali utuambie unataka tufanye nini kuhusu jambo hili."

decisions.choice: the king's treasure house: the royal archive where documents were kept
decisions.reason: Royal treasuries also stored official records. 6:1 calls it "the house of the scrolls" where the treasures were kept, and the scroll was finally found at Ecbatana (6:2).

decisions.choice: whether it is so: the officials neither deny nor accept the claim
decisions.reason: Tattenai does not accuse the Jews of lying; he asks the king to check. The question is left open for the king to decide, and the reply in chapter 6 settles it.

decisions.choice: his decision
decisions.reason: The king's "will" in a letter like this is his ruling on the case.

decisions.choice: if Your Majesty agrees, please
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the polite address of an official letter in plain words.

decisions.choice: "oh rey, si te parece bien" (R)
decisions.reason: Readable speaks to the king directly, as the English Readable does; the king is "tú" and "oh rey", as the terms note sets it, not "usted".

decisions.choice: "si tu es d'accord, ô roi"
decisions.reason: Readable addresses the Persian king as "tu" with "ô roi", as the letters do throughout the book, where the English Readable says "Your Majesty".
